emailSubject: FMB News | Taal Volcano Quakes Surge to 74 in 24 Hours; Alert Level 1 Kept | August 15, 2026 | 1:00 PM PHT
headline: Brief Reports 74 Volcanic Earthquakes at Taal; Alert Level 1 Remains
seoTitle: Brief Reports 74 Taal Quakes; Alert Level 1 Remains
seoDescription: An FMB News midday brief reports 74 volcanic earthquakes at Taal in 24 hours while Alert Level 1 remains in effect; the exact August 15 bulletin is still source-attributed.
deck: An FMB News midday brief reports a sharp increase in Taal seismic activity, while independently retrievable PHIVOLCS records continue to support Alert Level 1 restrictions and the permanent danger-zone warning.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The FMB News August 15 midday brief reports that Taal Volcano recorded 74 volcanic earthquakes during a 24-hour monitoring period, including 68 low-frequency events, and cites sulfur dioxide emissions of 4,288 tonnes per day.

FMB News could not independently retrieve the exact August 15, 2026 PHIVOLCS bulletin carrying those figures during the final publication pass. The 74-earthquake count, 68-event breakdown and 4,288-tonne sulfur-dioxide figure are therefore published as source-attributed newsroom-brief numbers, not as independently reproduced measurements.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Independently retrievable PHIVOLCS records from July 2026 show Taal under Alert Level 1, or low-level unrest, with entry into Taal Volcano Island prohibited and aircraft advised to avoid flying close to the volcano.
Those standing restrictions support the safety context of the report but do not independently establish the August 15 seismic and gas values.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Taal can produce sudden steam-driven or gas-driven explosions even during low-level unrest. Residents, visitors, boat operators and pilots need current PHIVOLCS guidance rather than recycled or date-mismatched volcano statistics.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for the corresponding August 15 PHIVOLCS volcano bulletin, updated sulfur-dioxide measurements, seismicity trends and any change to Alert Level 1 or access restrictions.
